newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-S&P puts News Corp on negative watch.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-S&P puts News Corp on negative watch.

text.p: Ratings agency Standard and Poor's Corp said on Thursday it had placed News Corp Ltd's BBB corporate credit rating and its BBB-r preference stock rating on credit watch with negative implications after the announcement of News' plan to buy International Family Entertainment for US$1.9 billion.
"IFE's principal asset, The Family Channel, is received by some 69 million subscribers and is a good strategic fit with News Corp's Fox Kids programming," S&P said.

"However, the price represents an extremely high multiple and, largely due to debt financing expected at the venture level, the venture will bE unable to generate net cash flow to its partners," S&P said.

"S&P will view News Corp as a critical source of support for the highly leveraged unit, especially given the company's contribution of its Fox Kids Worldwide interests to the venture and its strategic focus on programming content."

S&P also referred to the announcement that News would sell its U.S. satellite Direct-To-Home (DTH) assets to Primestar Partners in for US$1.1 billion of convertible preferred Primestar stock and convertible notes.
"This agreement extricates News Corp from the sizable investments and attendant risks in connection with its prior DTH business plan," S&P said.
Even before the IFE deal, News had little remaining debt capacity at the BBB corporate rating, it said.

News had pre-tax, interest and abnormal earnings (EBITA) to interest cover of 2.9 times in the year to March 31, 1997, and EBITA to interest and preferred dividends cover was 2.8 times after the acquisitions of New World Communciations and Heritage Media Corp.

S&P said News' cash and investments currently exceeded US$2 billion and the group had made progress with its US$800 million asset sale programme, which was expected to be completed over the medium term.

"Standard & Poor's expects that cash balances will be used, in part, to fund new business investments including the Fox Channel and the company's global DTH interests, which in aggregate are likely to continue requiring funding support over at least the next one to two years."
News' plans to buy the Los Angeles Dodgers for US$300 million would contribute little or no cash flow, but would strengthen its sports programming operations, S&P said.
"S&P currently expects that a reduction, if any, in the rating to be limited to one notch, which would leave the corporate credit rating at BBB minus.
"Further progress with asset sales to reduce debt could result in an affirmation."
S&P said a further review of financial policies would be part of the CreditWatch resolution.
News' shares were up 33 cents at A$6.20 at 11.10 a.m. (0100 GMT).
